title: High-fidelity streaming bench for connection churn and token-flow
creator: Nina Kapoor
description:
Goal: deliver a next-gen load driver that reproduces realistic streaming chat/completions at scale for both SSE and WebSocket protocols. This harness must exercise tokens/sec, idle/active session churn, multiplexing, prefix/KV cache hits, and p95 token-emit latency while producing deterministic regression signals for CI and on-call alerting.

Motivation: our current synthetic drivers emphasize raw RPS but underrepresent session churn, partial responses, and KV cache effects. Customers see regressions in p95 streaming latency under real-world churn that our tests miss. This ticket builds a bench that closes that blind spot and integrates regression gating into our perf pipeline.

Non-goals: simulating full upstream network path (we can use traffic shaping but not full WAN emulation), end-to-end client UX polish. Focus is server-side serving/runtime metrics and realistic session behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- The harness can spin up 10k concurrent simulated clients across multiple region emulators (configurable) and sustain mixed workloads (short chat, long completion, multi-turn).
- Emits token-level telemetry: per-request tokens/sec, per-connection p95/p50 token-emit latency, KV cache hit ratio, and backpressure events; metrics are exportable to Grafana/Prometheus with tags for protocol, model-variant, sequence-length-bucket, and tenant.
- Regression detection: nightly baseline runs compute stable p95 baselines and publish alerts when > 10% regression with statistical significance (bootstrap method). Alerts create a GitHub issue template and Slack runbook link.
- Replayer mode: take production-like trace files and replay sessions preserving timing and token interleaving; replayer supports session-rate scaling and seed control for determinism.
- Canary gating: integrate with CI to block runtime-2.4 canary rollouts if streaming p95 regression is detected for canary traffic sample.
- Lightweight chaos knobs: configurable connection drop rates, TLS renegotiation events, intermittent bandwidth throttling to reproduce tail behaviors.

Planned implementation approach:
1) Driver core: Go-based harness that manages connection pools, per-connection state machine (idle -> prompt -> token-stream -> idle), and supports both SSE & WS transports. Use efficient goroutine/shard model to reach high concurrent counts without blocking.
2) Token flow engine: a token scheduler that simulates real typing cadence (bursty vs steady), supports partial message stops, and models KV cache warm/ cold sequences.
3) Metrics & tracing: instrument with OpenTelemetry spans for start-of-stream, first-token, and end-of-stream; expose Prometheus counters and histograms for token latency buckets with labels.
4) Regression pipeline: data ingestion job that normalizes nightly runs, computes bootstrapped confidence intervals, and writes findings to our perf-dashboard service.
5) Replayer: converter that ingests production trace snippets (PSI format) and maps them to driver sessions; supports variable replay scale and seed for re-runs.

Artifacts and references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFER/Realistic+Streaming+Bench+v2
- Initial proto and spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-driver/pull/412 (DO NOT MERGE; spike)
- Perf dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming-bench/streaming-bench-overview
- Regression runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFER/Streaming+Bench+Regression+Runbook

Risks and trade-offs:
- Using heavy realism increases test fragility (false positives). Mitigation: baseline stabilization (30-run window) and multi-metric signals (p95 + error rate + kv-hit change).
- Running 10k concurrent TLS connections is resource-heavy; we'll provide an option to use TLS offload stubs for nightly CI and full-TLS for pre-prod.

Next steps:
- Finish driver core spike and open ENG RFC for metric schema (due 2026-02-26).
- Demo mid-stage harness in Cycle 54 demo (target 2026-03-05).
- Wire up nightly regression job and Slack alerting (target 2026-03-12).
